battle.name: 薛舉起事
battle.brief: 大業十三年四月，薛舉於長安西聚眾反隋，自號西秦霸王，旋稱帝遷都秦州。薛仁杲承襲後與唐軍相持涇水，武德元年七月李世民在淺水原以精騎破其大將宗羅睺，圍城斷糧，薛仁杲出降被誅，薛氏覆亡。短柄長刃、配鐵鏃的亞述長矛，正是關中步騎矛槊的形制遠祖；此役仍靠矛槊、弓弩與騎兵衝鋒定勝負。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries:
大業末年的關中，捲入兩股已經成形、一股正在成形的軍事力量。第一股是薛舉的西秦政權。薛舉原是河東郡汾陰縣人，父輩徙居金城郡，靠交結關中、河西的游俠與豪強起家，四月聚眾於長安以西，自號西秦霸王，置官屬、定年號秦興，七月稱帝並遷都秦州，以隴右為根據地，向東爭奪關中。他的部隊不是單一族裔的隊伍：關中與隴右漢族豪強的私兵、流入關中的流民編為步卒，羌、吐谷渾一帶的邊地部眾與馬匹提供騎兵，餘眾擔任輜重與守禦。薛舉病逝後，其子薛仁杲以秦王承襲，關中正面對唐的任務全交給大將宗羅睺的驍騎。

第二股是隋朝中央與關中官僚系統的殘餘。隋煬帝自大業六年以後遠巡江都，禁軍主力多調往江南與前線，關中只餘郡縣守兵與臨時湊集的募兵，靠屈豆通一類將領據守蒲城等堅城節制，弓弩當關、閉門待援，一路由樞密院與行台臨時調度。

第三股是李淵父子在太原起兵後組成的唐軍。李淵以晉王名義入關中，三月克長安、把隋恭帝楊侑握在手中，隨後以關中倉廩與渭水水道為後方，世民總兵權節制關中戰事。同一時期河北有竇建德、洛陽有李密、代北有劉武周、夏州有梁師都各自立號，隋朝的編制與調度在關中已名存實亡；此役記載之所以零碎，正因交戰雙方的指揮系統都在崩解與重建之中。
countriesEn:
In the closing years of the Daye era the Guanzhong basin was pulled into two military forces that had already taken shape and a third that was still forming. The first was the Western Qin regime of Xue Ju. Xue Ju was a native of Fenyin County in Hedong Commandery, and his father's generation had moved to Jincheng Commandery; he built his standing on ties with wandering knights and local magnates in Guanzhong and Hexi. In the fourth month he gathered a following west of Chang'an, proclaimed himself the Hegemon-King of Western Qin, established an apparatus of offices and set the era name Qinxing; in the seventh month he assumed the imperial title and moved his capital to Qinzhou, using Longyou as his base and pushing east into Guanzhong. His army was not ethnically uniform: the private retainers of Han magnates in Guanzhong and Longyou, together with refugees who had drifted into the capital region, formed his infantry, while frontier communities of the Qiang and Tuyuhun supplied his cavalry and horses; the remainder served as baggage train and garrison. After Xue Ju died of illness his son Xue Rengao succeeded as King of Qin, and the task of meeting the Tang head-on in Guanzhong was left to the cavalry of his general Zong Luohou.

The second force was what remained of the Sui central government and the Guanzhong bureaucracy. After the sixth year of Daye the Sui emperor Yang Guang had toured Jiangdu and did not return; much of the imperial guard had been shifted south and to the northern fronts, leaving in Guanzhong only county militia and hastily assembled recruits, controlled by commanders such as Qu Dutong who held fortified towns like Pucheng, with crossbows at the gates and a policy of staying shut and waiting for relief, directed in a makeshift way by the Secretariat and the regional headquarters.

The third was the Tang army formed after Li Yuan rose at Taiyuan. Li Yuan entered Guanzhong in the style of the Prince of Jin, took Chang'an in the third month and kept the Sui puppet emperor Yang You in his hand, then made the granaries of Guanzhong and the Wei River waterway his rear, while Li Shimin held the military command over operations in Guanzhong. At the same time Dou Jiande in Hebei, Li Mi at Luoyang, Liu Wuzhou in northern Dai and Liang Shidu around the Xia prefecture each raised a banner of their own, so that the Sui order of battle and its chain of command had become nominal in Guanzhong. The fragmentary state of the record on this campaign is precisely because the command systems on both sides were simultaneously disintegrating and being rebuilt.
people:
薛舉是這場起義的中心人物。史載他六世紀生於河東郡汾陰縣，父薛汪一代遷居金城郡，幼年落魄嗜酒，長於交結豪傑，在長安與涼州一帶往來結納武人；大業年間關中饑荒、役繁，他利用既有的人脈迅速拉起一支自效的隊伍，四月宣布西秦霸王，七月即皇帝位、遷都秦州，年號秦興。

薛仁杲是薛舉的嗣子，承接父業後退守涇州一帶，仍以薛氏名號聚兵。他統兵謹慎而缺乏決斷，倚重大將宗羅睺的驍勇，把關中正面對唐的任務全權交出，終致在淺水原一戰失去主動。宗羅睺是薛軍最精銳的騎將，所部號稱十餘萬眾，性好輕進，渭水一線受挫後眾潰，餘部再起亦被唐將段志玄追破，是薛氏覆亡的關鍵一環。

唐方的主持者是李淵與李世民。李淵在太原經營多年，十一月起兵，三月入長安，用隋恭帝的名號穩住關中的名分；世民領兵出渭北，與劉文靜、宇文士及等參贊。劉文靜力主乘關中饑荒未至極點、敵軍新敗未整之際速戰，反對屯兵俟麥；宇文士及奉命以百餘騎挑羅睺，誘其出陣衝擊。唐將段志玄負責追擊殘部。隋方在關中最後的主將屈豆通據蒲城拒守，終以城降唐，關中遂告平定。
peopleEn:
Xue Ju is the central figure of this rising. The histories record that he was born in the sixth century at Fenyin County in Hedong Commandery, that his father Xue Wang's generation moved to Jincheng Commandery, that as a youth he was down on his luck, fond of wine, and skilled at winning over men of mettle, moving between Chang'an and Liangzhou gathering followers among martial men; in the years of the Daye era, with Guanzhong Hungry and the corvée heavy, he used that network to raise a self-supporting force in a few weeks, proclaiming himself Hegemon-King of Western Qin in the fourth month and, in the seventh, taking the imperial title, moving his capital to Qinzhou and setting the era name Qinxing.

Xue Rengao, Xue Ju's successor as his son, drew back to the district around Jingzhou after his father's death, still raising troops under the Xue name. He commanded cautiously but without decision, leaned wholly on the dash of his general Zong Luohou, and handed over the task of meeting the Tang in Guanzhong; that is why he lost the initiative at the battle of Qianshuiyuan. Zong Luohou was the finest cavalry commander in Xue Ju's army, commanding a force whose numbers were claimed to exceed a hundred thousand, and given to over-eager advances; after he was checked on the line of the Wei River his command broke up, and the remnants that rose again were hunted down and destroyed by the Tang general Duan Zhixuan. He was the hinge on which Xue Ju's fall turned.

On the Tang side the directors of the war were Li Yuan and Li Shimin. Li Yuan had worked the Taiyuan base for years, rose in the eleventh month, took Chang'an in the third month, and used the name of the Sui puppet emperor to hold legitimate authority in Guanzhong. Li Shimin led the army out across the north bank of the Wei River, with Liu Wenjing, Yuwen Shiji and others as his staff. Liu Wenjing argued for a quick decision while the famine in Guanzhong had not yet reached its worst and the enemy was still reorganizing after a recent defeat, against waiting for the wheat to ripen; Yuwen Shiji was sent with a hundred-odd cavalry to provoke Zong Luohou and draw him out into a charge; the Tang general Duan Zhixuan was given the pursuit of the broken remnants. The last Sui commander in Guanzhong, Qu Dutong, held Pucheng in refusal and finally surrendered the town to the Tang, and with that Guanzhong was settled.
kits:
這張卡上的兵器是亞述長矛：短柄、長刃、配鐵鏃，出土於尼姆魯德與尼尼微一帶的亞述宮殿浮雕所見，年代約在公元前九世紀，是兩河流域鐵器兵裝成熟的見證。亞述人把長矛與弓、斧、鎬、投槍搭配在同一支部隊的編制裡，矛兵在正面以短柄護身、貼身近戰，弓手在兩翼掩護，而鐵鏃讓矛從可投擲的短標槍變成能夠反覆刺擊的直兵。就兵器譜系而言，它是後世矛與槊的遠祖型，而不是關中任何一支軍隊的直接來源。

真正在關中使用的是南北朝以來定型的隋唐兵裝。步兵以長槊、戈、戟列陣，輔以腰刀與盾，遇騎兵衝擊時以蹲盾車與拒馬成列抵擋；騎兵以槊為主兵器、弓為副兵器，人甲與馬甲並用，自北魏以來的重裝騎兵傳統一直延續到隋代禁軍。唐軍在長安城內外還保有蹶張弩、臂張弩一類的強弓，以及雲梯、撞車、穴車等攻城器械：雲梯靠人力推上前城，撞車用於撞擊城門，穴車則是掩體下的掘進器具。糧秣靠牛車與渭水、黃河水運，一旦戰事拉長，馬匹、箭矢與糧食的消耗就會先於兵員耗盡。

就亞述長矛的形制而言，短柄與鐵鏃的搭配在隋代仍有痕跡：隋軍的拒馬槊、牙門旗下的近衛長矛，都沿用短柄利刃便於在密集隊形中揮展的思路；只是到了隋唐，長矛的柄已延長到丈餘，刃部也改成更利於捅刺的形制，並與刀、劍、槊並用，形成中國式的長兵器組合。
kitsEn:
The weapon on this card is the Assyrian spear: a short shaft, a long blade and an iron head, as preserved in the palace reliefs of Assyria found at Nimrud and Nineveh, dating from about the ninth century BC and marking the maturity of iron equipment in the two riverlands. The Assyrians matched the long spear with the bow, the axe, the pick and the javelin within a single tactical grouping: the spearmen fought in front with a short shaft held close for protection and fought at close quarters, the archers covered them from the flanks, and the iron head turned what could be thrown as a short javelin into a thrusting weapon that could be used again and again. In the lineage of weapons this is the remote ancestor of the later mao and shao, not the direct source of any army in Guanzhong.

What was actually used in Guanzhong was the Sui and Tang equipment that had been fixed in form since the Northern and Southern dynasties. Infantry formed up with long shao, ge and ji, supported by waist-swords and shields, and when cavalry charged they set up crouching shield carts and caltrops to take the shock. Cavalry carried the shao as its main weapon and the bow as its secondary, wearing both body armour and barding, continuing the armoured cavalry tradition that had run from Northern Wei to the Sui imperial guard. The Tang also still had the powerful crossbows at Chang'an, both the foot-tensioned and the waist-cum-manual type, and siege equipment such as scaling ladders, battering rams and covered excavation carts: the ladders were pushed up to the walls by manpower, the rams were swung against the gates, and the covered carts carried out digging under cover. Supplies came by ox-cart and by the Wei and Yellow River waterways, and once a war was prolonged the consumption of horses, arrows and grain would run out before the troops did.

As for the form of the Assyrian spear, the pairing of a short shaft with an iron head still left traces in the Sui: the juma shao of the Sui army and the close-guard long spears under the yamaden banners all follow the idea of a short shaft with a working blade, easy to swing in a dense formation. Only by Sui and Tang times had the shaft of the long spear been lengthened to more than a zhang, the blade had been reshaped for thrusting, and it was used together with the dao, the jian and the shao to form the Chinese combination of long weapons.
tactics:
關中是一片被渭水、涇水與梁山切開的盆地，道路沿河谷延伸，村鎮多築有夯土城牆，兵家取勝的先決條件因此是有城可守與水路可通。

薛軍的戰法是先取據點、再伺機東進。起兵之初眾寡不濟，薛舉沒有直撲長安，而是先取關中西部與隴右的縣城，據涇州、秦州為基地，控住渭水上游與關中糧道的西端，再以騎兵為主力向東掃蕩，攻城倚賴雲梯與穴道，把長安以西的隋軍據點逐個拔除；遇到屈豆通這類死守之將，便圍城待援，把攻城變成僵持。

隋軍守方以關城為依托：閉門不出，以弓弩、擂石、拒馬消耗進攻者，拖到中樞調兵北上。問題是江都的朝廷已無力北援，關中的援兵往往在半路被其他起義軍截斷，守軍孤立無援，最後不是潰散就是棄城。

唐軍的打法在淺水原一役中最能說明。進軍渭北後，李世民不急於攻堅：先以強弩與騎兵列陣於涇水兩岸，派人挑釁誘敵；羅睺恃勇出營追擊，唐軍以精騎反覆衝擊其側翼，一戰而潰。追擊到城下仍不急攻，而先斷糧道、圍城，再以受降之人入城說項，逼得薛仁杲出降。羅睺殘部再起時，段志玄率騎追擊掩殺，掃清殘餘。整體而言，這是以騎兵制勝、以圍城收功、以追殲定局的典型戰法，與關中糧荒、敵軍新敗的時機配合得當。
tacticsEn:
Guanzhong is a basin cut by the Wei River, the Jing River and the Liang hills; the roads follow the river valleys, and most villages and towns were built with rammed-earth walls. The first preconditions for a commander there were therefore a town that could be held and a water route that could be used.

Xue Ju's method was to seize fixed points first and then wait for the moment to push east. Too weak at the outset to strike at Chang'an directly, he took the counties of western Guanzhong and Longyou, made Jingzhou and Qinzhou his bases, held the head of the Wei River and the western end of the grain road into Guanzhong, and then swept east with cavalry as his main strength. For siege work he relied on scaling ladders and covered excavation, picking off the Sui strongholds west of Chang'an one at a time; when he met a defender such as Qu Dutong who meant to hold his ground to the end, he invested the town and waited for relief, turning assault into a deadlock.

The Sui defensive side built everything on the walled towns: gates stayed shut, and the assaulting force was bled by crossbows, stones rolled down from the walls and caltrops, while the besieged waited for the court to send troops from the north. The trouble was that the court at Jiangdu had no strength left to send north; relief columns for Guanzhong were often cut off on the way by other rebels, so the garrisons were isolated, and in the end they either broke up or abandoned their walls.

The Tang method is best seen in the fighting at Qianshuiyuan. After moving out across the north bank of the Wei River, Li Shimin did not rush the walls. He first drew up strong crossbows and cavalry along both banks of the Jing River and sent men out to provoke; Zong Luohou, trusting to his own valour, came out of his camp in pursuit, and the Tang cavalry struck repeatedly at his flank until his army broke in a single action. Even on reaching the town walls the Tang did not assault at once, but cut the grain road, invested the town, and then sent a man who had already come over to talk the garrison down, which is how Xue Rengao was brought to surrender. When Zong Luohou's remnants rose again, Duan Zhixuan led cavalry in pursuit and killed them off. In overall terms this was a textbook method: cavalry to win the action, investment to gain the town, pursuit to settle the outcome, timed well against the famine in Guanzhong and the enemy's recent defeat.
data:
時間線清楚可考：大業十三年四月薛舉起兵，七月稱帝並遷都秦州，618年初薛舉病逝，薛仁杲承襲；武德元年（618年）七月淺水原決戰，其後薛仁杲出降並被押送長安，約同年十一月被誅。同期隋煬帝大業十四年三月李淵入長安，五月隋恭帝楊侑遜位改元義寧。

兵眾方面，起義之初所聚不過萬餘人，數月之間聚至數萬；薛軍自報精兵十餘萬或眾二十萬一類數目，按通鑑的體例多屬夸張之辭，實際當在數萬之譜。唐軍在淺水原投入的騎兵以數千計，全軍兵力亦遠少於薛軍。

距離與地勢方面，淺水原在長安西北約五十餘里，涇水自西北斜穿關中匯入渭水，兩岸多為高岸；薛軍後方秦州至涇州、再至長安西北戰線的距離在數百里以上，全靠陸路與渭水轉運。

經濟方面，關中大饑，米斗至萬錢，壯者聚群為盜；唐軍入關後糧食由太原、河東及渭北調運，軍中因此屢議俟麥熟進軍。

傷亡方面，雙方都沒有留下可靠的傷亡數目；史籍只記宗羅睺一軍眾潰、薛仁杲出降、屈豆通以蒲城降唐，以及薛仁杲與諸子被誅。自617年4月起兵到618年秋降唐，西秦政權前後維持一年有餘，中經一場決戰與一次圍城。
dataEn:
The chronology is clear and can be checked: in the fourth month of the thirteenth year of Daye Xue Ju rose; in the seventh month he took the imperial title and moved his capital to Qinzhou; early in 618 Xue Ju died of illness and Xue Rengao succeeded him; in the seventh month of the first year of Wude (618) the battle of Qianshuiyuan was fought, after which Xue Rengao surrendered and was sent under escort to Chang'an, and was put to death around the eleventh month of the same year. In the same period, in the third month of the fourteenth year of Daye Li Yuan entered Chang'an, and in the fifth month the Sui puppet emperor Yang You abdicated, with the era name changed to Yining.

On numbers of troops, the rising began with little more than some ten thousand men and grew to several tens of thousands within a few months. The figure of more than a hundred thousand picked troops, or two hundred thousand men in all, claimed for Xue Ju's army is, in the usual judgement of the Comprehensive Mirror, an exaggeration; the real strength was in the range of several tens of thousands. The Tang cavalry committed at Qianshuiyuan numbered several thousand, and the whole Tang army was far smaller than the Xue army.

On distances and terrain, Qianshuiyuan lay a little over fifty li north-west of Chang'an, and the Jing River runs obliquely down through Guanzhong to join the Wei, with high banks on both sides. The distance from the Xue rear base at Qinzhou to Jingzhou, and from there to the north-western fighting line before Chang'an, ran to several hundred li and had to be covered entirely by road and by transfer on the Wei.

On the economy, Guanzhong was in severe famine, rice reaching ten thousand cash a dou, and the strong men gathered in bands to rob; after the Tang entered the pass, grain was brought up from Taiyuan, Hedong and the north bank of the Wei, and the army in the field argued more than once about waiting for the wheat to ripen before advancing.

On losses, no reliable casualty figures survive for either side. The records state only that Zong Luohou's command broke up, that Xue Rengao surrendered, that Qu Dutong handed over Pucheng to the Tang, and that Xue Rengao and his sons were executed. From the rising in the fourth month of 617 to the surrender in the autumn of 618 the Western Qin regime lasted a little over a year, with one decisive action and one siege in between.
cause:
要理解為何關中會在617年出現這樣一場起義，得從隋朝崩解的次序說起。

大業年間三次征伐高句麗，轉輸與徭役同時壓在關中，民間早已怨聲載道；大業六年以後，隋煬帝遠巡江都並長期不返，京師禁軍多被調往南方與北方戰線，關中只剩郡縣守兵與臨時募集的雜兵，屏障近乎空虛。關中連年失調、糧價飛漲，流民成群，地方豪強則有馬有糧有部曲，一遇亂局便能以招聚部曲、收納亡命的方式迅速成軍。

薛舉正是這樣的產物。他的出身在關中、河西的游俠與豪強之間，多年結交的都是可以出錢出馬出人的地方人物，起兵時喊出的西秦霸王既借了西部邊族的旗號，也給關中豪強一個改朝換代又不必投靠河北、洛陽的選項。

外部條件同樣重要：611年楊玄感已在黎陽起兵，其後河北有竇建德、洛陽有李密、代北有劉武周、夏州有梁師都，隋朝的命令在多數州縣已不再被執行。李淵在太原陰謀反隋，更把關中變成各方必爭之地，薛舉搶先在長安以西舉事，正是要在別家尚未染指關中之前，把關中的倉廩與關隘拿到手上。關中一旦落入他人之手，隴右的馬匹與關中的糧食就會變成對手的資源；這一點決定了此役不是單純的地方叛亂，而是一場爭奪全國樞紐的戰爭。
causeEn:
To understand why a rising of this kind should break out in Guanzhong in 617, one has to follow the order in which the Sui came apart.

During the Daye era, three campaigns against Goguryeo wore out the treasury, while the transport service and the corvée fell on Guanzhong at the same time, and resentment in the countryside had long been general. After the sixth year of Daye the Sui emperor toured Jiangdu and stayed away for good; much of the capital guard was moved south and to the northern fronts, so that in Guanzhong only county militia and hastily gathered irregulars remained, and the shield of the region was close to empty. Year after year the harvests of Guanzhong went wrong and grain prices soared, refugees gathered in bands, while the local magnates, who had horses, grain and private retainers, could raise a force in a few weeks by calling in their retainers and taking in men without a master.

Xue Ju was a product of exactly this world. His ties lay among the wandering knights and magnates of Guanzhong and Hexi, and the men he had known for years were precisely those who could supply money, horses and men. The title he proclaimed on rising, Hegemon-King of Western Qin, borrowed the banner of the western frontier peoples, and at the same time gave the magnates of Guanzhong a way to change masters without having to join Hebei or Luoyang.

The external conditions mattered just as much. Yang Xuanshi had already risen at Liyang in 611; after him came Dou Jiande in Hebei, Li Mi at Luoyang, Liu Wuzhou in northern Dai and Liang Shidu around the Xia prefecture, and in most prefectures and counties the orders of the Sui were no longer obeyed. Li Yuan's conspiracy at Taiyuan turned Guanzhong into a prize that every party had to fight for. By rising west of Chang'an first, Xue Ju was trying to seize the granaries and the passes of Guanzhong before any other power laid a hand on them. Once Guanzhong fell to another hand, the horses of Longyou and the grain of the region would become the resources of the enemy. That is what made this campaign more than a local rebellion: it was a struggle for the hinge of the empire.
impact:
此役結束時，關中的局勢已經徹底改觀。

第一是隋朝的崩解從事實上的失控變成法律上的滅亡。李淵三月入長安、五月奉楊侑退位，隋朝最後的名號只剩下對關中以外的空懸；薛氏覆亡則把關中西部與隴右一併納入新朝的版圖，使唐得以在同一時間內控制渭水、涇水兩條糧道與秦州、涇州等關中重鎮。

第二是關中作為帝國後方的格局被固定下來。此後近一個世紀，唐宋的西北邊防都以關中為基地，隴右的屯田、軍馬與糧秣輸送自此成為國家制度的常態；秦州一帶由割據者的巢穴變成唐經營吐谷渾與党項的前哨，天水至長安這條線上的驛站與城鎮多在這一時期定型。

第三是兵制與戰術層面的傳承。這一場戰役把重裝騎兵的作用推到極致：渭水線上，數千精騎的側擊擊潰號稱十餘萬的步騎大軍，隨後的圍城與追殲也由騎兵完成；隋唐以來的鎧騎傳統、槊與長刀並用的近戰組合、弩兵在守城與野戰中的位置，都在這幾個月的實戰中重新校準。

第四是關中人口與生產的消耗。圍城與追擊戰都發生在產糧區，米斗萬錢的饑荒不但沒有因戰爭結束而平息，反而因大批青壯被徵、被俘而更加嚴重；這正是唐初整頓戶籍、擴充屯田、推行租庸調的背景所在。起義軍與官軍的傷亡數字雖無可靠記載，但兩年之後唐廷仍要面對陝隴一帶糧價與戶口的嚴重問題，足見此役留下的消耗有多深。
impactEn:
By the time this campaign was over, the situation in Guanzhong had been completely transformed.

First, the collapse of the Sui changed from a collapse in fact into an extinction in law. With Li Yuan entering Chang'an in the third month and Yang You stepping down in the fifth, the last name of the Sui hung empty over everything outside Guanzhong; the fall of the Xue house meanwhile folded western Guanzhong and Longyou into the new dynasty's territory, allowing the Tang to hold the two grain roads of the Wei and the Jing and the key towns of Qin and Jingzhou at the same time.

Second, Guanzhong's role as the empire's rear was fixed in place. For close to a century afterwards the north-western frontier of the Tang and the Song rested on Guanzhong, and the garrison farms, the war-horses and the grain traffic of Longyou became a permanent part of the state system. The district around Qinzhou changed from a nest of separatists into the Tang's outpost for dealing with the Tuyuhun and the Tanguts, and the post-stations and towns along the line from Tianshui to Chang'an largely took their final form in this period.

Third, there was a legacy at the level of arms and tactics. The campaign pushed armoured cavalry to its extreme: on the line of the Wei River a flanking blow by some thousands of picked horsemen broke an army of infantry and cavalry claiming more than a hundred thousand, and the investment that followed and the pursuit of the broken were likewise carried out by horse. The armoured cavalry tradition of the Sui and Tang, the close-combat pairing of shao with long blade, and the place of the crossbow in both siege and field were all recalibrated in the hard fighting of these few months.

Fourth came the drain on the people and the produce of Guanzhong. The siege and the pursuit both took place in the grain-growing country, and the famine at ten thousand cash a dou was not settled by the end of the war but made worse, since large numbers of young men were conscripted or taken captive. That is the background to the early Tang's work of registering households, expanding garrison farms and putting the rent, labour and commutation system into order. No reliable casualty figures for the rebels or the government troops survive, yet two years later the Tang court was still confronting serious problems of grain prices and population in the Shaan-Gan region, which shows how deep the drain of this campaign went.
result:
武德元年七月的淺水原，是西秦與唐之間的定案之戰。薛仁杲倚宗羅睺的精騎列陣於渭水，恃勇輕進，被唐軍精騎乘勢掩殺，主力一潰而不可收拾；唐軍隨即追至城下，圍城斷糧，又以段志玄追破羅睺再起的殘部。薛仁杲在無援可恃的情況下出降，被押送長安，其後與諸子一同被誅，西秦政權自此覆亡。關中方面，隋將屈豆通最終以蒲城降唐，涇水兩岸的隋朝防務瓦解。

若只看關中，這是一場乾淨的勝利：薛氏多年累積的部眾與關係網被連根拔起，隴右重新回到中央控制之下，唐朝取得了一個完整而未經戰火太過焚毀的關中基地。但放回隋末的大棋盤，它只是第一步。

整場起事自617年4月至618年秋，前後不過一年有餘，卻把關中這個決定性的舞臺推到了天下爭奪的前景。此後劉武周於619年南下太原、王世充於619年據洛陽稱帝、竇建德雄據河北，唐廷仍需再花二十年才完成統一。薛舉起事真正的意義在於：它證實了關中可以被奪取，也證實了只要守住涇水與渭水的渡口、讓騎兵取得決定性的側擊，就足以瓦解一支人多勢眾的割據軍；這套經驗，後來在唐滅夏州、平定梁師都與吐谷渾的戰役中一再重演。而亞述長矛那種短柄長刃、配鐵鏃的形制，在這個關中戰場上早已化為矛與槊的形制傳統，隨每一支結陣的步兵與每一隊衝鋒的騎兵，在渭水兩岸的塵土裡延續下去。
resultEn:
The fighting at Qianshuiyuan in the seventh month of the first year of Wude was the case that settled Western Qin against the Tang. Xue Rengao had massed the picked cavalry of Zong Luohou along the Wei River; trusting to his valour he pressed forward in over-confidence and was cut down by the Tang horse, and his main force broke in a way it could not be restored. The Tang pursued to the walls, invested the town and cut its grain road, and Duan Zhixuan again destroyed the remnant that Zong Luohou tried to raise. With no relief possible, Xue Rengao came out and surrendered, was taken under escort to Chang'an, and was later executed together with his sons, and with him the Western Qin regime disappeared. On the Sui side, Qu Dutong finally handed Pucheng to the Tang, and the Siu defensive line along the Jing came apart.

Judged in Guanzhong alone, this was a clean victory: the retainers and the network of relationships the Xue house had built over years were torn out by the root, Longyou returned to central control, and the Tang gained a base in Guanzhong that was whole and not too badly scorched. Set back on the larger board of the late Sui, however, it was only the first step.

The rising as a whole lasted a little over a year, from the fourth month of 617 to the autumn of 618, yet it pushed Guanzhong, that decisive stage, to the forefront of the contest for the empire. Liu Wuzhou came south against Taiyuan in 619, Wang Shichong seized Luoyang and proclaimed himself emperor in the same year, Dou Jiande held the Hebei plain, and the Tang court still needed another twenty years to complete the unification. The real significance of Xue Ju's rising lies in the fact that it proved Guanzhong could be taken, and that by holding the crossings of the Jing and the Wei and letting cavalry win the decisive flanking blow, a numerically far larger separatist army could be broken. That lesson was acted on again and again in the Tang campaigns that destroyed the Xia prefecture and settled Liang Shidu and the Tuyuhun. And the form of the Assyrian spear, a short shaft, a long blade and an iron head, had long since become part of the form tradition of the mao and the shao; on this Guanzhong field it went on in the dust along both banks of the Wei, with every infantry column that closed ranks and every troop of horsemen that charged.
